speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you recall any specific injury or insect bite at the onset?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (erythema migrans misidentified as wrist pain or concurrent Lyme arthritis with tenosynovitis).

This diagnosis is based on the patient's recent camping trip in Minnesota, the 3-day history of worsening wrist pain with fever and chills, and the preceding self-resolving knee pain, which is highly suggestive of disseminated Lyme disease. I will now confirm if the skin lesion on the wrist is expanding or ring-shaped.
